findings.problem: `who` said authority is re-proved inside the claim and the completion. The completion re-proves no authority. complete runs acceptPaymentExecutionInTx and then completePaymentCommandSubmissionInTx, which calls submitAcceptedPaymentCommandInTx. That function skips the authorizePaymentCommandSubmissionInTx guard that its sibling submitPaymentCommandInTx runs. The only owner check is the command's originatingAuthUserId.
findings.evidence: packages/backend/src/payments/writes/ledger.ts:71 (sibling runs the guard) vs ledger.ts:86-110 (no guard); commands/writes/submissions.ts:99-101; executions/writes/acceptances.ts:22-68

findings.problem: It said a claim the call did not win 'is sent only if the bundler already holds the hash'. That is backwards. A claim it did not win is never sent: if hasUserOperationByHash is true it goes straight to completion, otherwise it fails SUPERSEDED (unobservable-claim). The text also left out that a row refused before dispatch answers that refusal, and that an already accepted row goes straight to completion.
It said a prepared Attempt whose sponsorship lapsed is classified and refused SUPERSEDED. It is refused only when the classify mutation actually writes an outcome. Otherwise the send goes on.

No record drove machine_payment_command_verification. recordSubmission sets verificationState 'scheduled', and a bound landed own operation also sets 'scheduled'. Sponsorship expiry resets it to 'not_started'. Added to_scheduled to complete, and to_scheduled plus to_not_started to classify, both sends and the sweep.

It was missing the birth transition. storePreparedExecutionInTx inserts the row in state 'prepared', and data.ts's machine_money_execution.t.to_prepared cites this exact line. It drove only to_expired.

The scheduled branch's touches were missing, although the actions' touches are meant to be the union of their internal steps. That branch runs payments.schedules.load-command (Permissions' readBudgetAllowanceInTx) and payments.schedules.store, which drives machine_payment_schedule.t.to_waiting and projects through loadPaymentDocuments. Added that transition and both procedures.

The Permissions authorize procedures were missing. The public submit accepts any execution the caller owns, and the claim's authorizeClaimInTx authorizes a Permission or invitation execution through Permissions, so that path is reachable. The about now records that such an execution is claimed and sent, and that complete then refuses it with INVALID_INPUT.
findings.evidence: executions/writes/claims.ts:103-105; schedules/external.ts:114 (scheduled branch returns null for non-payment); executions/writes/acceptances.ts:34-36

findings.problem: It said a Payment command that already ended is refused with WRONG_STATE. A failed command is INVALID_INPUT (requestFailed, field requestKey); only other endings are WRONG_STATE. The about also omitted that a row whose preDispatchOutcome is own_lane_advanced is claimed like any prepared row. `who` left out the Board-approved schedule caller, and its Permissions reference pointed at the import line instead of the call.

It listed every refusal as WRONG_STATE. A missing command is INVALID_INPUT (commandNotFound), and a failed one is INVALID_INPUT (requestFailed) after the authority check. The about also omitted that an unsent prepared Payment Attempt of an ended command does not hold the lane.

It said false is answered only when the execution moved or was already refused. Fail also answers false when the Payment command already ended or was applied (recordPaymentCommandOutcome). The nested payments.commands.load-execution-context step, which raises INVALID_INPUT for another person's execution, was not named.

It said the unheld page reads rows 'with no hold'. The index key is recoveryCheckAt === undefined, so a hold recorded before that key existed still arrives in the unheld sweep, where recoveryDue filters it.
It omitted the own-lane resolution caller in a build (resolveAdvancedOwnLane).

Its errors list the admitted ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED, SMART_ACCOUNT_MISSING and ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, but no path in complete raises them. I kept the admitted list, which is what the code declares, and recorded in the about that no path raises them and that money writes switched off give NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

priority 'critical' is the writer's judgement: the code sets no priority. The sibling verifications.ts books the cron that runs this sweep inline (payments.verifications.recover-job) as 'normal', so the child is ranked above its own trigger. Left unchanged because no code fact decides it; it needs a ruling.
timeoutMs 600000 and retries {max:0} are Convex platform defaults, not values the code sets. The about already says so. The schema requires both fields, so they were kept.

designFindings: Complete re-proves no authority, although the code says it does. transactions.ts:15-26 says 'Recording re-proves the caller's authority' and admits ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED, SMART_ACCOUNT_MISSING and ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. But submitAcceptedPaymentCommandInTx (writes/ledger.ts:86) skips the guard that submitPaymentCommandInTx (ledger.ts:71) runs. The comment is stale and the error codes are dead. Authority is checked only at claim time, then trusted through the bundler round trip.

Payments' public submit and submitCommand send another concept's operation and then refuse it. A Permission or invitation execution passes the claim (claims.ts:103-105, through Permissions' guards), goes to the bundler (sends.ts:151), and complete then answers INVALID_INPUT 'is not a Payment execution' (acceptances.ts:34). The Attempt stays `sending` until the claim sweep completes it through Permissions (recoveries.ts:90-95).

One action composes about 8 separate Convex functions with no transaction across them: load, classify, reset-claim, claim, record-send-attempt, complete, schedules.load-command and schedules.store (sends.ts:98-189, schedules/external.ts:107-140). Correctness rests on fences each mutation re-checks: state, hash and claim token (classifications.ts:239-245, holds.ts:37-41).

Misleading name and stale doc: reset-claim releases no claim. Its own docstring still says 'release the claim for a later retry' (operations/reset-claim.ts:12), while the writer says no reset exists (writes/claims.ts:189-206).

The own_lane_advanced diagnostic does not block a claim. preDispatchRefusal returns SUPERSEDED for it (errors.ts:34-39), but claimSubmissionInTx short-circuits only on ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED and WRONG_STATE (claims.ts:139-140). Only the preflight's fresh lane read stops such a send, and the preflight is skipped for a non-prepared row (sends.ts:124-127).

Boundary breaks. Payments writes Banking through deep imports: acceptPayoutQuoteInTx (executions/writes/claims.ts:12, :182) and payoutSendFailedInTx (writes/outcomes.ts:5, :108). The wire Payment projection reads the accounts, identities, orgs and counterpartyDestinations tables directly (views/recipients.ts:75, :80, :88, :109). The claim authorizes Permission executions with Permissions' guards (claims.ts:7-8).

Error codes are overloaded. An ended (failed) command is INVALID_INPUT on field requestKey (commands/errors.ts:18-22), while other endings are WRONG_STATE (errors.ts:194-199). A signer's refusal is WRONG_STATE with currentState '<state>:signer_refused' (errors.ts:44-52). Every SUPERSEDED reason (sponsorship-expired, lane-advanced, unobservable-claim, stale-nonce) names executions.submitCommand as the operation even when submit raised it (errors.ts:55-165).

Duplicated helpers. 'Money execution not found' is built by executionNotFound in errors.ts:182, again in reads/executions.ts:19, and inline in claims.ts:137 and acceptances.ts:32; acceptances.ts:85 says 'Payment execution not found' instead. The ended-command refusal is checked separately at store admission (commands/writes/links.ts:81-95) and at claim (claims.ts:101-102).

'Active' means two things. loadActiveExecutionInTx treats a `succeeded` Payment execution as active (reads/executions.ts:35-39), but store's one-live-execution check uses activeExecution alone (writes/stores.ts:48).

The claim sweep has no overlap guard. It reschedules itself with runAfter(0) per full page under the first cutoff (recover-claims.ts:69-80), while the 10-minute cron (platform/jobs.ts:87-93) can start a new first run meanwhile. Two runs can read the same rows; only per-row fences keep the writes single. The cron exists only when money writes are on and a V2 address is set (jobs.ts:87).

Telemetry is a scheduled function inside the money transaction. scheduleWriterTelemetry runs a payment_transitioned emitter from every Payment writer (events/writer.ts:72); store attaches a 'prepared' progress event (commands/writes/links.ts:128), complete a 'pending' one (commands/writes/submissions.ts:168-175).
